prompt: Two parallel railroad rails are crossed by a straight service road (a transversal). One interior angle measures $105^\circ$. What is the measure, in degrees, of the co-interior angle — the one between the rails, on the same side of the road?
hint: Co-interior (same-side interior) angles are not equal — they are supplementary.

hints.text: Co-interior (same-side interior) angles are not equal — they are supplementary.

explanation: Co-interior angles (also called same-side interior or consecutive interior angles) lie between the parallel lines on the same side of the transversal.
When the lines are parallel, those two angles are supplementary: they add to $180^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Two steps you already know
steps: The $105^\circ$ angle has an alternate interior partner across the road, also $105^\circ$.
That partner and the angle you want form a linear pair along the rail: $180 - 105 = 75^\circ$.
